title: Technical English — Course 4, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 10

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the security lesson take place?
tasks.audioText: The control systems tutor will discuss information security principles on Tuesday at two. Students should meet in the project classroom and bring the security glossary. The lesson will cover account access, approved software updates and reporting unusual activity. It will focus on responsible documentation and will not include practical access to live control systems.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which course resource should students bring to the security lesson?
tasks.audioText: The control systems tutor will discuss information security principles on Tuesday at two. Students should meet in the project classroom and bring the security glossary. The lesson will cover account access, approved software updates and reporting unusual activity. It will focus on responsible documentation and will not include practical access to live control systems.

tasks.prompt: Control systems documentation should identify approved software versions and the roles permitted to access system information. Unusual activity should be reported through the organisation's approved process. Staff should not share account credentials or install unapproved software. Clear records help a technical team understand what changed and which authorised person or process was involved. Reading 1. What should control systems documentation identify?
options: Approved software versions and permitted access roles

tasks.prompt: Why should unusual activity be reported?
options: So the technical team can understand what changed and who or what process was involved

tasks.prompt: Unusual activity should ___ through the approved process.
Choose TWO responsible practices for control-system information security.
Information that proves who accessed or changed a system may form an audit ___.
A colleague asks you to share your account password. What should you say?
options: I will send it in a message.
I cannot share credentials; please use the approved access process.
I will write it on a public notice.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of information security in control systems in a logical order.
options: Report unusual activity through the approved process
Use the authorised account and software
correctOrder: Use the authorised account and software
Report unusual activity through the approved process

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words describing responsible information-security practices for a control-system team. Include access, approved software and reporting.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: task completion and relevant content (0–2); clear organisation and logical linking (0–2); grammar and sentence structure (0–2); accurate technical vocabulary, spelling and punctuation (0–2). Minor errors are acceptable if meaning remains clear.
